resources.name: Crash Course Computer Science
resources.why: A friendly tour of the whole field, from switches to AI. No coding needed, so it works before you have written a single line.

resources.name: roadmap.sh: Computer Science
resources.why: A clickable map of how CS topics connect. Read it for orientation, not as a to-do list.

resources.name: CS50x Week 0: Scratch
resources.why: What computing actually is, taught with drag-and-drop blocks before any typing.

resources.name: Learning How to Learn
resources.why: How memory, focus and procrastination really work. The highest return per hour on this whole map.

resources.name: So You Want to Be a Wizard, by Julia Evans
resources.why: A short illustrated zine on how to get good at not understanding things yet. Perfect first read.

resources.name: Download Python
resources.why: The official installer. Get the latest version 3 release.

resources.name: Visual Studio Code
resources.why: The editor most students and professionals use. Free, and it runs on any laptop.

resources.name: VS Code: Getting started with Python
resources.why: The official walk-through: install, write hello world, press run.

resources.name: CS50P, Harvard's Introduction to Programming with Python
resources.why: Harvard's Python course for people who have never coded. Free, brilliantly taught, with problem sets that are graded automatically. This is the one course for the Python line.

resources.name: CS50P Lectures (official playlist)
resources.why: The same lectures on YouTube, if you prefer watching there. Watching is not learning, so do the problem sets too.

resources.name: CS50P Week 0: Functions and Variables
resources.why: Lecture, notes and problem set for your very first Python.

resources.name: CS50P Week 1: Conditionals
resources.why: if, elif, else and match, with a problem set.

resources.name: CS50P Week 2: Loops
resources.why: while, for, lists and dictionaries in loops, with a problem set.

resources.name: CS50P Week 3: Exceptions
resources.why: What to do when things go wrong, on purpose and by accident.

resources.name: CS50P Week 6: File I/O
resources.why: Reading and writing files, including CSV spreadsheets.

resources.name: CS50P Final Project
resources.why: Build anything you like in Python, with clear requirements to aim at.

resources.name: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition
resources.why: Practical Python: files, spreadsheets, web pages. Every chapter ends with something that does a real job for you.

resources.name: Python Tutor
resources.why: Paste your code and step through it line by line, watching every variable change. The cure for 'why is my loop doing that'.

resources.name: Invent Your Own Computer Games with Python
resources.why: Learn by building small games, from Hangman to Tic-Tac-Toe. By the author of Automate the Boring Stuff.

resources.name: Advent of Code
resources.why: A yearly set of story puzzles. The first few days are beginner friendly, and every past year stays playable.

resources.name: Project Euler
resources.why: Maths-flavoured programming puzzles. Problems 1 to 20 are a lovely way to get fluent. It gets hard quickly after that.

resources.name: LeetCode
resources.why: Interview practice. It assumes you already know data structures. Bookmark it and come back in a year or two.

resources.name: Adel Nasim: Learn C++ Programming From Scratch, in Arabic
resources.why: The C++ course Egyptian CS students recommend most. In Arabic, from zero.

resources.name: Elzero Web School: Before You Learn Programming
resources.why: An Arabic primer on what programming is and how to approach learning it.

resources.name: LearnCpp.com
resources.why: The most thorough free written C++ tutorial. Read the chapter that matches what you are stuck on.

resources.name: Missing Semester: The Shell
resources.why: A one-hour introduction to the terminal, with exercises.

resources.name: The Linux command line for beginners
resources.why: A gentle written walk-through of the terminal. The same commands work on a Mac.

resources.name: Learn Git Branching
resources.why: A game that draws the Git history as you type commands. The only resource that makes Git visible.

resources.name: Git and GitHub Crash Course for Beginners, freeCodeCamp
resources.why: From nothing to working on a shared project, in one sitting.

resources.name: GitHub Docs: Hello World
resources.why: The official ten-step first project on GitHub.

resources.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack
resources.why: Free professional tools for verified students. Apply with your university email as soon as you have one.

resources.name: How to ask good questions, by Julia Evans
resources.why: A short, kind guide to asking technical questions that get answered.

resources.name: Rubber Duck Debugging
resources.why: Explain your code, line by line, to a rubber duck. You will find the bug before the duck answers. This is a real technique.

resources.name: CS50: notes on using AI
resources.why: How Harvard's course thinks about AI helpers: a tutor that guides you is good, a machine that does your homework is not.

resources.name: CS50 Duck (cs50.ai)
resources.why: An AI tutor built to nudge you toward the answer instead of handing it over.

resources.name: Julia Evans' blog
resources.why: The friendliest writing anywhere on how computers, networks and the terminal really work.

resources.name: CS Unplugged
resources.why: Computer science ideas taught with cards, string and games. No computer required.

resources.name: Khan Academy: Algorithms
resources.why: Searching, sorting, recursion and Big-O, with interactive exercises. The gentlest real introduction.

resources.name: Intro to Algorithms, Crash Course Computer Science #13
resources.why: What an algorithm is and why some are faster than others, in one episode.

resources.name: CS50x Week 3: Algorithms
resources.why: Searching, sorting and Big-O, acted out on stage with real people.

resources.name: CS50x Week 5: Data Structures
resources.why: Linked lists, trees and hash tables explained from the ground up.

resources.name: VisuAlgo
resources.why: Watch sorting, trees and graphs run as animations, on your own input.

resources.name: Big-O Cheat Sheet
resources.why: One chart showing how fast the common algorithms and data structures are.

resources.name: What on Earth is Recursion? Computerphile
resources.why: Recursion explained calmly, with a whiteboard.

resources.name: Abdul Bari: Algorithms
resources.why: Everything worked out by hand on a whiteboard. The standard rescue when an algorithms course gets hard.

resources.name: MIT 6.006, Introduction to Algorithms
resources.why: A rigorous university algorithms course, taught in Python. For when you want the real thing.

resources.name: 3Blue1Brown: Essence of Linear Algebra
resources.why: Linear algebra as moving pictures. Three hours that make a whole course easier.

resources.name: 3Blue1Brown: Essence of Calculus
resources.why: What derivatives and integrals actually mean, shown visually.

resources.name: Professor Leonard: Calculus 1
resources.why: Patient, complete classroom lectures. He explains everything three ways.

resources.name: Khan Academy: Linear Algebra
resources.why: Vectors and matrices with worked practice.

resources.name: Khan Academy: Maths
resources.why: Every school maths topic, for filling gaps such as logarithms or probability.

resources.name: Discrete Mathematics: An Open Introduction, by Oscar Levin
resources.why: A discrete maths textbook written for first-years, with hundreds of exercises, hints and solutions.

resources.name: Book of Proof, by Richard Hammack
resources.why: The book that teaches you how to write a proof, the skill most students find hardest.

resources.name: Kimberly Brehm: Discrete Math
resources.why: A full discrete maths course in short lectures, following the most common university textbook.

resources.name: TrevTutor
resources.why: Short worked examples in discrete maths: logic, sets, proofs, counting.

resources.name: Sebastian Lague: Exploring How Computers Work
resources.why: Calm, beautiful videos building up from logic gates to a working adder.

resources.name: Digital Logic Sim, by Sebastian Lague
resources.why: A free simulator for wiring up your own logic gates and chips.

resources.name: Ben Eater: Build an 8-bit computer from scratch
resources.why: A working computer built from chips on breadboards, one wire at a time. You do not need to build it to learn from it.

resources.name: Core Dumped
resources.why: Clean animated explanations of what a process is, how memory works and what the operating system does.

resources.name: Branch Education
resources.why: Stunning 3D animations of real hardware: inside a chip, a CPU, a hard drive.

resources.name: Nand to Tetris
resources.why: Build a whole computer, from one logic gate up to a game running on it. No prior knowledge required, just patience.

resources.name: Shimon Schocken: The self-organizing computer course (TED)
resources.why: The creator of Nand to Tetris on why building a computer from scratch changes how you see the field.

resources.name: Code, by Charles Petzold: companion site
resources.why: Interactive circuits from the most enjoyable book on how computers work. The book is worth asking for as a gift.

resources.name: Khan Academy: Computers and the Internet
resources.why: Binary, how computers are built, and how the internet moves data, with exercises.

resources.name: MDN: How does the Internet work?
resources.why: A short, clear article on what actually happens between your laptop and a website.

resources.name: FcisHub
resources.why: A student-built hub for your faculty: past exams, lecture material, schedules and staff contacts.

resources.name: FCIS Ain Shams ICPC Community
resources.why: Your faculty's problem-solving community. Runs beginner training from zero. New rounds usually open around October to November, with another intake in the mid-year break.

resources.name: GDG on Campus, Ain Shams University
resources.why: Google's student developer community on campus. Beginner friendly, and you can attend events with just an RSVP.

resources.name: FCIS Student Union
resources.why: Student families, trips, sports and cultural activities. The easiest way to meet people in the first weeks.

resources.name: MSP Tech Club, ASU
resources.why: A student tech community with technical tracks and non-technical committees. Recruits once a year, usually around October, by form and interview.

resources.name: OSC, Open Source Community
resources.why: Founded in your faculty in 2013. Teaches tracks such as Linux and software engineering from scratch. Recruits in autumn.

resources.name: IEEE Ain Shams Student Branch
resources.why: Technical committees, workshops and events, based in the Faculty of Engineering next door. Ask whether your faculty's students can join.

resources.name: GDG Cairo
resources.why: Cairo's Google developer community. Runs DevFest Cairo, usually in December, and Google I/O Extended, usually in June.

resources.name: Women Techmakers Cairo
resources.why: Google's women-in-tech community for Cairo. The main event is around International Women's Day, usually March to April.

resources.name: NASA Space Apps Cairo
resources.why: A two-day hackathon, usually in autumn. No experience needed. Teams want designers and storytellers as well as coders.

resources.name: CyberTalents competitions
resources.why: Hosts Egypt's national cybersecurity capture-the-flag, usually around January, online, and open to beginners.

resources.name: Egypt Game Developers
resources.why: The community behind Global Game Jam in Egypt, usually late January. Beginners and students are welcome.

resources.name: Egypt Game Developers on Discord
resources.why: A moderated Discord server for Egyptian game makers, artists and students.

resources.name: Arab Dev Hub on Discord
resources.why: An Arabic-speaking developer community for beginners and professionals.

resources.name: Mahara-Tech
resources.why: Free courses in Arabic from the Information Technology Institute, with certificates. No application, start any time.

resources.name: ITIDA and NTI free summer training
resources.why: A government summer programme that lists first-year computer science students as eligible. Registration usually opens around June.

resources.name: ITI summer training
resources.why: The Information Technology Institute's free summer camp for undergraduates, in branches across Egypt. Applications usually open around May to June.

resources.name: Software Internship Guide for Egyptian Undergraduates
resources.why: A community list of internships in Egypt. Most open from third year, so star it now and use it later.

resources.name: Adel Nasim
resources.why: Full Arabic courses in C++, data structures and Java.

resources.name: Elzero Web School
resources.why: Very organised Arabic courses, with a written study plan for each one.

resources.name: The Coding Train
resources.why: Joyful creative coding. He makes mistakes on camera and fixes them live, which is the most reassuring thing you can watch.

resources.name: p5.js
resources.why: Draw and animate with code in your browser. It is JavaScript, and it is for play.

resources.name: Sundas Khalid
resources.why: A self-taught data scientist on learning tech skills and building a career, from a non-traditional background.

resources.name: Rewriting the Code
resources.why: A large international community for university women in tech, with mentorship and events. Open to first-years.

resources.name: Grace Hopper Celebration
resources.why: The world's largest gathering of women in computing. Student scholarships exist. Worth knowing about for later years.

resources.name: Google scholarships
resources.why: Google's scholarships for computer science students, including a Europe, Middle East and Africa edition.

resources.name: CS50P Week 4: Libraries
resources.why: Using code that other people wrote: random numbers, statistics, and talking to websites.

resources.name: CS50P Week 5: Unit Tests
resources.why: Writing small programs that check your program, so bugs get caught before you do.

resources.name: CS50P Week 8: Object-Oriented Programming
resources.why: Classes and objects, introduced gently with clear examples.
